title: Choose the visual world for the Case IQ landing page
question: The roll assigned The Card Catalogue. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Card Catalogue
options.lineage: public-library card catalogues and the reference desk
options.thesis: Every fact is a card, and every card has a call number: the page it came from.
materials: white index cards with blue rules
coral, sky and mint guide tabs
options.viewport: A wall of oak drawers; the top drawer slides toward you, its front card carries the headline, guide tabs are the case-type choices, and the next card is the proof: your words, the quoted line, and its call number.
options.risk: Reads nostalgic or library-only if the oak and type are timid, and younger visitors may never have used a card catalogue, so the index card itself must carry it.

raised.raise: Every layout snaps to whole card units, and a gap is a designed blank card stamped 'Not in your papers yet', never an empty space.
Leader lines pin each claim to its source card, so every reference is drawn, not just listed.
The intake is one card filled field by field, with a discrete step counter and Next as the default action.
The card in hand is at full strength while the rest of the drawer steps back, still readable.
Selected evidence is marked by shape, an outline around the quoted words, never by tint alone.
Figures and page numbers sit in fixed tabular positions, and the drawer's card count ticks up as the pile is filed.

options.label: The Expanding File
options.lineage: the pressboard accordion file people buy for their case
options.thesis: The accordion file you bought for your case, finally working for you.
options.viewport: The file seen from above with its elastic snapped open; the headline sits on the front sheet, tabs are the case-type choices, and picking one pulls that example sheet up with its proof.
options.risk: The most literal reading of 'organize your papers', so it is the familiar choice, and brown pressboard can feel dated.

options.label: Azulejo Station Hall
options.lineage: tin-glazed tile halls in Portuguese railway stations
options.thesis: Your case painted across tiles, with every tile a page.
options.viewport: A tiled hall where the timeline runs across framed panels and a missing page is a blank white tile.
options.case: Fuses well on gaps, but most Ontario visitors won't recognize the form, and its clarity trails the catalogue's call numbers.
options.kept: A whole-unit grid, and a designed blank for what's missing.
options.risk: Reads as travel or decor rather than help with a court case.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: A case as forces held in balance.
options.viewport: A floating column of rods with every claim tied by cord to its counterforce.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a balance of forces implies weighing who is right, which Case IQ never does.
options.kept: Leader lines that pin each claim to its source.

options.label: Shareware Installer
options.thesis: Getting help as a step-by-step setup wizard.
options.viewport: A setup dialog with Back and Next, a progress bar, and the intake as wizard pages.
options.case: Fuses for the intake only; it trivializes a court case and says nothing about sources.
options.kept: One field at a time, discrete progress, and Next as the default.
options.risk: Reads as a joke or as outdated software.

options.label: Glyph-Rain Terminal
options.thesis: Your papers resolving out of falling data.
options.viewport: Falling green characters that lock into your timeline where you look.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dark-and-neon AI imagery is exactly what frightens this audience.
options.kept: Focus discipline: only the item in focus is at full strength.
options.risk: Feels like hacking or surveillance, and its motion is hard to make accessible.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: Every paper opens as a window on one desk.
options.viewport: A dithered desktop with your papers as windows and the quoted line selected.
options.case: Fuses for 'see the page' but reads as retro computing, not as case help.
options.kept: Selection marked by shape, never by tint alone.
options.risk: Novelty with little warmth for stressed visitors.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Your case counted out in glowing digits.
options.viewport: Tube banks counting the pages read and the events found.
options.case: Fuses for figures only, and numbers aren't what visitors need to believe.
options.kept: Fixed tabular figures and counts that change visibly.
options.risk: A cold instrument look that implies metrics we don't publish.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What consumer legal-help sites ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and button on the left, a timeline screenshot on the right, and a trust row below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other legal-tech sites by design.
